title: Wind power physics
summary: How wind speed sets the power available to a turbine (cube law), how much a rotor can capture (Betz limit), and how a real farm's power curve departs from both.

concepts.label: Wind farm
concepts.description: Westermost Rough: 35 Siemens SWT-6.0-154, 210 MW, off the Holderness coast.

facts.text: Elexon BMRS B1610 gives metered generation per BM unit per settlement period.
Westermost Rough was the first commercial use of the 6 MW, 154 m rotor turbine (2015).

children.label: Power curve
children.description: Output against wind speed: cut-in, cubic rise, rated plateau, cut-out.

children.label: Wake losses
children.description: Turbines downwind see slower, more turbulent air; part of the gap below Betz.

children.label: Curtailment
children.description: Output reduced on instruction (grid constraints); not in this data.

concepts.label: Power in the wind
concepts.description: P = ½ ρ A v³ through the swept area A.

facts.text: Wind power density scales with the cube of wind speed.

children.label: Cube law
children.description: The exponent of output against wind below rated power.

children.label: Air density
children.description: ρ = p/(R T): colder, denser air carries more power at the same speed.

children.label: Wind speed distribution
children.description: How often each speed occurs; with the cube law it decides where the energy comes from.

concepts.label: Betz limit
concepts.description: The maximum power coefficient of an ideal rotor, 16/27 ≈ 0.593, from momentum theory.

facts.text: Albert Betz derived the limit in 1920.

concepts.label: Pitch control
concepts.description: Turning the blades to spill power above rated wind speed, which caps output.

concepts.label: ERA5 reanalysis
concepts.description: ECMWF's hourly reanalysis on a 0.25° grid, served by Open-Meteo.

facts.text: Open-Meteo's historical weather API serves ERA5 under CC BY 4.0.
